sights.w: Six floors of modern and contemporary art holding Van Gogh's Starry Night, Monet's Water Lilies, and a landmark design and film collection.
The 1932 Art Deco showplace inside Rockefeller Center, home of the Rockettes and the largest indoor theater of its era.
A 22-acre Art Deco complex with the golden Prometheus fountain, seasonal ice rink, and the Channel Gardens promenade.
A Neo-Gothic Roman Catholic cathedral of white marble on Fifth Avenue, its twin spires rising 330 feet opposite Rockefeller Center.
The 1930 Art Deco skyscraper with a stainless-steel sunburst crown, long a candidate for the city's most beautiful tower.
A formal green behind the main library with a carousel, free lawn games, a winter rink and holiday market, and cafe kiosks.
A block-long food hall in the former Nabisco Oreo factory, packed with vendors, tacos, seafood, and specialty shops.
Renzo Piano's tiered Meatpacking building with terraces over the Hudson, showing American art from the Whitney's deep 20th-century collection.

sights.address: Pier 55 at W 13th St, New York, NY 10014
sights.w: A public park on tulip-shaped concrete pods rising over the Hudson, with rolling lawns, overlooks, and a summer amphitheater.
Daniel Burnham's 1902 triangular terracotta tower wedged where Broadway crosses Fifth Avenue; a defining view (exterior only, under residential conversion).
The West Village site of the 1969 uprising, the first U.S. national monument to LGBTQ history, with Christopher Park and an NPS visitor center.
The only NYC museum devoted solely to fashion, with a research-grade costume collection and free rotating exhibitions.

sights.address: Madison Ave & E 23rd St, New York, NY 10010
sights.w: A leafy Flatiron square with rotating public art, dog runs, and the original Shake Shack kiosk under the trees.

sights.address: Union Square W & E 17th St, New York, NY 10003
sights.w: The city's flagship farmers market since 1976, drawing regional growers and top chefs four days a week to Union Square.
A gated cobblestone lane of former 19th-century carriage houses just north of Washington Square, once home to Edward Hopper.
James Renwick Jr.'s 1846 French Gothic Revival masterpiece and National Historic Landmark where Broadway bends at 10th Street.
The city's only 19th-century family home preserved intact, its 1832 rooms filled with the Tredwell family's original furnishings.
The Western Hemisphere's highest outdoor sky deck, a triangular platform jutting 80 feet out at the 100th floor with a glass floor.

food.w: Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse mashing up KBBQ and an American chophouse, grilling dry-aged USDA Prime tableside.
Jody Williams and Rita Sodi's beloved rustic West Village gastroteca known for market vegetables and handmade pastas.
Danny Meyer's Michelin-starred seasonal-American institution; the front tavern room is walk-in and serves its famous burger.
Family-run Ukrainian diner in Little Ukraine since 1954, open late for pierogi, borscht, and potato pancakes.
Coal-oven pizzeria since 1915 serving whole pies only, no slices, from an 850-degree brick oven in the West Village.
Two-story Koreatown mainstay built around bubbling stone bowls of soft-tofu stew with banchan and cast-iron rice.
The first U.S. outpost of the Japanese chain, its rich pork-bone broth a benchmark for the city's ramen boom.
Brooks Headley's Bib Gourmand vegetarian burger counter turned sit-down diner, with cult veggie burgers and gelato.
Michelin-starred Emilia-Romagna osteria in the Flatiron built on handmade pasta and a regional tasting menu.
Chef Hoyoung Kim's Michelin-starred Korean fine-dining room offering an approachable, grill-forward tasting near Flatiron.
A tiny Michelin-starred Gramercy tapas bar, Costa Brava-inspired, with adventurous plates and a wall of sherry.
East Village Filipino kitchen from chef Eric Valdez serving regional comfort dishes and a communal kamayan spread.
Udon specialist on Curry Row where the chef hand-cuts thick, chewy noodles for hot and cold bowls plus chawanmushi.

food.dish: Natural wine and seasonal small plates
food.w: An intimate East Village natural-wine bar with 250-plus bottles, orange-wine depth, and vegetable-driven counter cooking.
Eyal Shani's Israeli street-food stall inside Chelsea Market stuffing charred pita with cauliflower, lamb, and steak.
